name: FIVE CARD STUD
description: Five Card Stud is one of the earliest forms of Stud Poker, emerging in the mid-19th century. Unlike Draw Poker, Five Card Stud is an 'open' game where most of a player's hand is visible to everyone at the table. Each player receives one hidden 'hole' card and four exposed 'up' cards, with betting rounds interspersed between each deal. This creates a high-tension environment where players must calculate their strength against the visible threats in their opponents' hands.

content.text: Five Card Stud is one of the earliest forms of Stud Poker, emerging in the mid-19th century. Unlike Draw Poker, Five Card Stud is an 'open' game where most of a player's hand is visible to everyone at the table. Each player receives one hidden 'hole' card and four exposed 'up' cards, with betting rounds interspersed between each deal. This creates a high-tension environment where players must calculate their strength against the visible threats in their opponents' hands.

Five Card Stud rose to prominence during the American Civil War, evolving from earlier forms of Poker as a way to provide more information and betting opportunities per hand. It was the standard casino Poker variant for decades before being largely supplanted by Seven Card Stud in the mid-20th century.
Cards are dealt one at a time. The first card is face-down, subsequent cards are face-up.

items.text: Fifth card face down: The fifth card is dealt face down so only three cards are visible in the last betting round; first to act in that round is the same as the previous round.

Lowball: Lowest hand wins. Ace counts low. First betting round often started by highest card showing (bring-in); subsequent rounds by lowest hand showing. Standard low hand ranking (e.g. ace-to-five or ace-to-six) used at showdown.
Five Card Stud High-Low: Pot split between highest and lowest hands; declaration (high or low) after final betting; odd chip to high. Often 8-or-better for low.

Sökö (California Stud): Same as Five Card Stud except two extra hand ranks below a pair: 4-straight (four consecutive ranks plus odd card) and 4-flush (four of one suit plus odd card). Hand order: high card, pair, 4-straight, 4-flush, two pair, three of a kind, straight, flush, full house, four of a kind, straight flush.
